description_html:
An orthopaedic dog bed has one job: to carry your dog's weight evenly so their hips, elbows and shoulders never press through to a hard floor. That takes dense, supportive foam that keeps its shape, not fibre that flattens. Most sizes are listed in centimetres, and every bed here comes with a 100-night trial.

How to choose an orthopaedic dog bed

What makes a dog bed genuinely orthopaedic

The word isn't regulated, so plenty of beds use it loosely. Run three checks. The base should be solid foam rather than loose fill. It should be deep enough that your dog doesn't sink to the floor. And it should recover its shape after they get up. Try the fist test: press your fist into the centre. If you can feel the floor, so can your dog. The Grasmere, a memory foam dog sofa with three cushioned bolsters and an open front, is a good place to start.

Who an orthopaedic bed is for

Large and giant breeds, older dogs, dogs who are stiff after exercise, and any dog who has abandoned their bed for the floor because it has gone flat. If your vet has advised firmer support, start here and ask them which shape suits your dog. To browse by size, see large dog beds and extra large dog beds, or by life stage, dog beds for older dogs.

Is an orthopedic dog bed the same as an orthopaedic one?

Yes. Orthopedic is the American spelling and orthopaedic is the British one. It's the same idea: a supportive foam bed that keeps your dog off the floor.

Will an orthopaedic bed help my dog's arthritis?

A bed can't treat arthritis, and your vet should lead on that. What a supportive bed can do is stop a stiff dog sinking through to a hard surface, and a low, easy entry means lying down and getting up take less effort. See our low step-in dog beds. Prefer a softer, moulding feel? Compare memory foam dog beds, or browse all dog beds.
claims_to_confirm: 'Foam cores, not loose filling' is true of all 37 members at writing (Appendix A: every one is memory foam, egg-crate or layered foam; Langdale says 'orthopaedic foam' and Patterdale 'a foam core'). The collection is a smart collection (type 'Dog Beds > Orthopaedic Dog Beds' OR tag 'orthopaedic dog bed'), so a future fibre-filled product with that tag would make the line untrue. Keep the tag for foam beds only.
'Most sizes are listed in centimetres' (not 'every'): Patterdale's description and size labels give no measurements, and Haweswater's XL has none. Add them and the line can say 'every'.

The audit deck's 'Every bed sized in cm with breed and weight guides' and 'Every bed says which [foam]' were not used as written: breed and weight guides exist on only a few variants (custom.suits_breeds / suits_weight), and Langdale and Patterdale do not say whether their foam is memory or egg-crate (custom.core_type blank). The intro says 'Each bed's page says what's inside' instead.

5-year no-flatten guarantee applies to 23 of the 37 members (custom.foam_guarantee true); not Langdale, Nocturne, Bowfell, Braithwaite, Burnmoor, Easedale, Esthwaite, Newlands, Patterdale, Scafell, Glaramara, Honister, Loughrigg, Mungrisdale. The SEO description says '5-year memory foam guarantee', which is accurate for the memory foam beds only.

'A good place to start' now points at Grasmere (memory foam, best seller per audit S06) instead of Nocturne (egg-crate), per audit COL-15. 'The fist test' is not linked yet: link it to the 15-second foam video once filmed (COL-15).

Manual order per audit COL-05: Grasmere, Ambleside, Coniston, Langdale, Nocturne, then the remaining memory foam beds (core_type Memory foam or Crumb memory foam) by lowest variant price high to low (ties: highest price, then title), then the egg-crate beds the same way, with Patterdale (core type unstated) last. New members added by the smart rule go to the end until re-sorted.
Ennerdale's second product image carries on-image text 'CertiPUR-US Certified' and 'Reversible design'. Neither is in the product data. Confirm the certification (with evidence) or replace the image.
Nocturne's fourth product image carries on-image text beginning 'ULTIMATE COMFORT FOR...'. Superlative not supported by the data; consider replacing.
Ambleside's product photos appear to show a rimmed, nest-style bed, while the description says edge-to-edge mattress with 'no soft rim' and 'no walls'. Confirm the photos show the product sold.

Handle/title mismatches worth tidying with redirects (audit Appendix C): rosthwaite-xl-waterproof-orthopaedic-bed, the-loweswater-orthopaedic-bolster-dog-bed (Melbreak), the-kentmere-orthopaedic-bolster-dog-bed (Staveley), wasdale-xxl-orthopaedic-sofa-bed (Burnmoor).
